sections.kicker: Prepared for TONE. by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: TONE. promises a way of living. The site opens on a T shirt joke.
sections.keep: Your hashtag, "#setthetone." It turns the name into something people do.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.quote: WHEN LIFE GIVES YOU LEMONS... SHOP THE LEMONADE TEE!
pins.what: The site greets people with a one tee drop and a lemon pun.
pins.why: For more sales, the front door has to sell TONE. first; a single tee sells one tee.
pins.how: Lead with the movement and comfort idea, and let each drop sit under it.
pins.label: Your site
pins.cost: Visitors who miss this tee leave without knowing what TONE. is.

pins.what: The bio lists three categories instead of one stance.
pins.why: Many activewear labels claim movement, wellness and comfort; none of it says why TONE.
pins.how: Pick the one belief behind TONE. and say it in plain words.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: TONE. gets compared on price with every activewear label that writes the same line.

pins.what: The hashtag already does what the bio does not.
pins.why: It turns the name into an action people can join.
pins.how: Build the site and the grid around setting the tone, not around drops.
pins.label: Your hashtag
pins.cost: The strongest owned idea stays a tag at the end of a caption.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on TONE.'s own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
